observations: Single photo shows a black cylindrical moving-head stage light with a circular lens and white trim ring, sitting on a white box/surface.

identity.kind: LED moving head beam light (stage/event lighting fixture)

claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows a fixture consistent with this type, but no power-on or beam test is visible.

claims.claim: stage & event lighting (implying working/functional for such use)
claims.evidence: No photo or clip shows the unit powered, moving, or producing a beam.

risks.risk: Unit may not power on or the LED/lamp may be dead.
risks.proof: A photo or short video of the fixture plugged in and lit, ideally with the beam visible.

risks.risk: Moving head motors (pan/tilt) may be stuck or noisy.
risks.proof: A video clip showing pan/tilt movement during a DMX or test mode cycle.

risks.risk: Lens or internal optics may be cracked, cloudy, or water-damaged.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the lens from the front and any internal glass/mirror.
risks.if_unproven: priced as cosmetically/functionally damaged until shown clear

risks.risk: No visible model/brand plate means wattage, LED count, and feature set (DMX channels, beam angle) are unknown, which affects comparables.
risks.proof: A clear photo of any rating label, sticker, or nameplate on the housing.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a generic/unbranded low-spec unit

risks.risk: Missing accessories (power cable, DMX cable, clamp, manual) could add cost for buyer.
risks.proof: A photo of all included accessories laid out next to the unit.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unit only, no accessories

proof_requests: Video of the fixture powered on, showing it light up and the pan/tilt motors moving.
Close-up photo of any brand/model/rating label on the housing.
Close-up photo of the lens and internal optics for cracks or fogging.
Photo of included accessories (cable, clamp, manual, box).
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable by type as a LED moving head beam light, but no functional test, label, or accessory photos are shown, so it must be priced at worst case as a non-working, unbranded unit until proof is provided.
